The mess we're solving

Your fridge, your inbox, and your head are all equally full.

Recipe sites assume you have the energy to choose. Most nights, you don't.

Symptom 01Stressed, but every recipe assumes you're in a great mood.
Symptom 02Groceries bought with intention, tossed out with guilt.
Symptom 03What you actually need isn't a recipe — it's ten quiet minutes.
How MoodBake works

Three steps between "I can't decide" and dough in the oven.

01

Answer 11 quick taps

Big buttons, honest emoji, no typing. Each answer quietly tags your mood and your budget.

02

Get three matches

The system pulls three recipes from its library that fit your tags — nothing you have to filter yourself.

03

Bake, timer included

Start the built-in Zen Timer, breathe for twenty minutes, and let the oven do the rest.

What's inside

Five small tools, built to remove one decision each.

The Mood Quiz

Eleven questions, one match.

Multiple-choice, icon-led, built for a foggy brain. Behind the scenes, every answer carries a tag — "stressed," "low-budget," "craving chocolate" — and the quiz simply retrieves the three recipes that share your tags.

😩 Stressed
💸 Low budget
🍫 Craving chocolate
⏱ 30 min or less
🥣 One bowl only
Pantry Matcher

What's actually in your kitchen?

Tap what you have. See only recipes that use it.

Baking Zen Timer

Twenty minutes to just breathe.

14:02

A calm countdown with soft facts about baking chemistry and a built-in lo-fi playlist, so the oven timer doubles as a reset.

Budget Toggle

Only show what you can afford.

The Surprise Me Button

No energy for eleven questions? Fine — we'll pick.

One random, responsibly comforting bake — chosen for you, no questions asked.
